reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern consists of sharp, near-vertical upward transitions from baseline (robust-standardized value ≈ 0.0) to a plateau at ≈2.47, followed by equally sharp downward transitions back to baseline, forming rectangular pulses. Each pulse spans approximately one estimated period (≈50 points), with consistent amplitude (90th-percentile amplitude ≈2.47) and zero median/MAD across all candidates, indicating no offset or scale drift. Pulses are well-separated by flat baseline segments; inter-pulse spacing varies but is always ≥~30 points in the longer windows. No discernible trend, curvature, or noise—signal is piecewise constant with near-zero roughness. In the 5-period window (candidate 3), five identical pulses appear with uniform width (~12–13 points high edge, ~12–13 points low edge, ~25–26 points plateau), confirming periodic repetition without deformation. Boundary truncation is absent: all pulses are fully contained within their windows, and edges align cleanly with integer indices. Acceptable variation includes minor jitter in exact transition timing (±1–2 points) and negligible slope in plateau (≤0.02 per point), but any deviation from rectangular morphology—e.g., rounded edges, partial pulses, or sustained non-zero baseline—is anomalous.

Always match pulse count and relative timing, not absolute x-index.
